newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates stay firm on fund outflow.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates stay firm on fund outflow.

text.p: Interbank rates stayed firm on Monday, helped by some fund outflows following intervention by Bank Negara Malaysia in the foreign exchange market, dealers said.
"There's an outflow today from Bank Negara's forex intervention but we're not sure about the size," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Banking sources said the central bank sold an estimated $400 million last week to defend the ringgit.
Dealers said they expected interbank rates to stay firm due to a one-billion ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Tuesday.

Rates started firming on Friday after a surge in swap points, triggered by rumours of a Bank Negara meeting with bank chief executives to discuss the possibility of introducing selective capital controls to defend the ringgit.
But banking sources said there was no such meeting.
Dealers said certain large commercial banks were seen lending on the one-month with some suspecting that it was on behalf of Bank Negara.
One-week money was at 7.30/50 percent against 7.00/50 percent on Friday.
One- and three-month money were at 7.50/80 percent against 7.50/60 percent.
The overnight rate, which ended at 5.80/90 percent on Friday, was expected to trade around 6.0 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were marginally higher.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up two to 92.57, or an implied yield of 7.43 percent.
The December contract rose three to 92.73, or 7.27 percent and March 1998 was up two to 92.76, or 7.24 percent.
